question: to the Commission Sander Smit (ECR), Jessika van Leeuwen (ECR) Subject:

POLITICO1 has recently revealed that almost 1 000 written complaints have been received by the European Commission’s confidential counsellors since 2024. These reports cover topics including verbal and physical harassment by managers, humiliation, high workload and fear of repercussions when submitting complaints. However, the counsellors themselves have no authority to investigate. This raises questions about the internal administrative culture within the European Commission and how complaints are followed up. The EU is founded on democracy, equality and respect for human dignity. It is therefore very important that these values are respected and protected within the European institutions too. 1.
What concrete measures is the Commission taking to systematically combat verbal and physical harassment and abuse of power by managers?
Is the Commission willing to report annually and transparently on the nature of the reports, and what guarantees are there of diligent and independent follow-up?

What is the Commission’s assessment of the risk that reports of verbal and physical harassment, abuse of power and inadequate handling of complaints could harm the confidence that European citizens have in the European institutions and the credibility of the EU?

Starcevic S., 1,000 complaints made to European Commission’s anti-harassment team, POLITICO, 6 August 2026, https://www.politico.eu/article/1000-complaints-european-commissions-anti-harassment-team/. 1
